q: In ESLint, which severity makes the run fail?
why: Only an error makes the linter exit with a failure code; a warning is just reported.

q: Why keep lint rules in a config file in the repo?
o: Editor, teammates and CI all use the same settings
why: One shared file means no surprises between your editor and CI.

o: # noqa: F401 with a note on why
Turning the rule off for the whole repo
why: Naming the rule hides only that rule, and the reason tells the next reader it's still needed.

o: a saved list of old findings that are no longer reported
the first line of a config file
why: New code must be clean while old findings are fixed when someone touches them.

q: Your first lint run gives 2,000 findings. Best first step?
o: Fix them all in one big change
Turn on only bug rules, auto-fix the safe ones, baseline the rest
Make every rule a warning forever
why: Starting small avoids a huge risky change and doesn't block everyone's commits.

q: Making every rule an error is the safest setup.
why: Myth: if everything fails the run, people stop reading the output; keep errors short and real.
